answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring each new identity to extract a unique ferrous relic from a shared glacier whose extraction rate is physically capped per epoch. The relic locks as stake and must be countersigned by an established peer who also freezes matching capital. If peer grading detects correlated behavior across the glacier face, every locked relic in that cohort is slashed. An attacker needs a separate independent sponsor plus a scarce extraction slot for every extra fake; once the glacier fills, further clones wait behind real agents who will not risk capital for a farm.
